contexts.text: (On those who have made jokes from the Word.) AC 1878. SE 1304.
That he derided. Signified. For with those who are in no charity, there is a continual contempt, or continual derision, of others.
That external worship separated from internal is such that it derides. Signified.
It would mock at or ridicule this.
Where evils are, there they are mocked at.
He did not appear with a face, but only as to the teeth, because he had been able to mock at others...
He would laugh at all who attributed these things to the Divine.
Without this use, the evil utterly ridicule truths.
The simpler Spirits... laughed at them... The reason of their derision was soon disclosed...
Conjoined with contempt for others, enmity, ridicule...
